Check Sampler Validity and Render Diagnostic Plots

Source: R/profile_check_sampler.R
profile_check_sampler.Rd

The numeric half of "did this Stan run actually work": checks the standard HMC/NUTS validity criteria (divergences, max-treedepth hits, E-BFMI, split-Rhat, bulk/tail ESS) against widely used thresholds from the Stan/posterior documentation, and renders the three standard diagnostic plots (trace, rank, energy) via bayesplot – the same mcmc_trace()/mcmc_rank_overlay() functions already used elsewhere in anumaan (plot_worst_offender_diagnostics.R), plus mcmc_nuts_energy() for the energy check that file doesn't currently render.

Usage

profile_check_sampler(
  fit_result,
  rhat_max = 1.01,
  ess_min = 400L,
  ebfmi_min = 0.2,
  variables = NULL,
  output_dir = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  derived_estimates = NULL,
  mcse_budget = NULL
)

Arguments

fit_result

The list returned by profile_fit_joint_bernoulli (reads $fit, $summary, $diagnostics), or a raw cmdstanr CmdStanMCMC object (summary/diagnostics are then computed fresh from it).

rhat_max

Numeric. Split-Rhat above this value fails a parameter. Default 1.01 (Vehtari et al. 2021's revised threshold).

ess_min

Integer. Bulk or tail ESS below this fails a parameter. Default 400L (the Stan-documented minimum for stable 95 interval estimates).

ebfmi_min

Numeric. E-BFMI below this, per chain, fails that chain. Default 0.2 (Betancourt 2017's threshold).

variables

Character vector or NULL. Which parameters' Rhat/ESS to check and plot. Default NULL: every parameter in the summary except lp__.

output_dir

Character or NULL. If supplied, writes sampler_check.rds (status/reasons/checks, not the plot objects) and each plot as its own PDF into this directory.

ci_level

Numeric in (0, 1). Credible-interval level the quantile-MCSE checks (both mcse and derived_mcse) are computed at. Default 0.95 (MCSE of the 0.025 and 0.975 quantiles – posterior::mcse_quantile()'s ess_tail() alone summarizes a DIFFERENT combination of tails and does not replace checking the actual interval endpoints you report).

derived_estimates

Named list or NULL. Each element a numeric matrix of posterior draws (n_draws x n_quantities) for a DERIVED estimand not among variables – e.g. per-hospital resistance probabilities from profile_estimate's class_probability_draws/profile_probability_draws, reshaped to one column per hospital x class/state. When supplied, mean and quantile MCSE are computed per column and returned as derived_mcse – raw sampler diagnostics on beta/ eta do not by themselves say whether a DERIVED probability is precise enough to report. Default NULL (skipped). NOTE: unlike mcse (computed on the fit's own chain-aware draws), derived_estimates columns are treated as one pooled sequence – profile_estimate does not track which chain each subsampled draw came from, so no between-chain correction is applied here; this MCSE is a reasonable, slightly optimistic approximation, not the exact chain-aware quantity mcse reports.

mcse_budget

Numeric or NULL. The MCSE budget each derived_estimates column's mean and quantile MCSE is checked against – e.g. 0.1 * epsilon, where epsilon is the approved probability half-width target (a project convention, not something this function derives). NULL (default): MCSE is still reported, just not pass/failed against anything. Extending sampling addresses a numerically UNSTABLE estimate (MCSE too wide for the budget); it does NOT make a long but genuinely imprecise scientific interval (wide because of real data/model uncertainty) narrower – these are different problems, and this check only diagnoses the former.

Value

A list:

status

"pass", "warning", or "fail". "warning" means only ESS (precision, not sampler validity) failed to clear ess_min; any divergence, treedepth, E-BFMI, or Rhat failure is "fail". MCSE-budget failures (on derived_estimates) do NOT affect status – they are a separate, reporting-level judgment the caller makes explicitly, not a sampler-validity verdict.

reasons

character vector of failed checks' names (empty when status == "pass")

checks

data frame, one row per check: check, value, threshold, status

mcse

data frame, one row per variables entry: variable, mcse_mean, mcse_lower_quantile, mcse_upper_quantile (at ci_level's endpoints)

derived_mcse

empty (zero rows) unless derived_estimates is supplied; one row per (estimate name, column): estimate_name, column, mcse_mean, mcse_lower_quantile, mcse_upper_quantile, budget, passes_budget (NA when mcse_budget is NULL)

plots

list of 3 ggplot objects: trace, rank, energy

Details

This is deliberately upstream of any scientific judgment about the MODEL (calibration, held-out performance, which classes/panels to trust) – those are profile_ppc, profile_validate_masked, profile_validate_heldout, and profile_sensitivity (elsewhere in this family). A sampler can pass every check here and still fit a badly miscalibrated model; this function only answers whether the SAMPLER did its job, which is a precondition for trusting anything downstream of it.
